images.filename: Gravestones - geograph.org.uk - 407115.jpg
images.caption: Gravestones The graveyard of St Mary's Cardigan is orderly with graves in neat rows and older gravestones lined along the wall. The occupations of the dead convey a picture of  the town as a place where ships and sea dominated C19 life: mariner, shipwright, sailmaker, ropemaker, blockmaker...

images.filename: Ceinewydd, Ceredigion, Cymru (Wales) - Mehefin 2024 - 15.jpg
images.caption:
Ceinewydd, Ceredigion had 1,082 inhabitants in the 2011 Census, 41% of whom spoke Welsh (down from 47% in 2001). The A486 connects it to Llandysul and Carmarthen. It stands halfway between Aberystwyth and Cardigan. (From cywiki)
Ceinewydd (translation: New Quay), Ceredigion.

SAC Special Areas of Conservation: West Wales Marine and Cardigan Bay / Bae Ceredigion.
